Q22923830.label: 2020 United States presidential election
Q22923830.summary: Presidential elections were held in the United States on November 3, 2020. The Democratic ticket of former vice president Joe Biden and California junior senator Kamala Harris defeated the incumbent Republican President Donald Trump and Vice President Mike Pence. The election saw the highest voter turnout by percentage since 1900.

Q380982.label: Emilio Portes Gil
Q380982.summary: Emilio Cándido Portes Gil was a Mexican politician, lawyer and diplomat who served as the 48th President of Mexico from 1928 to 1930, one of three to serve out the six-year term of president-elect General Álvaro Obregón, who had been assassinated in 1928. Since the 1917 Constitution forbade re-election of a serving president, incumbent President Plutarco Elías Calles could not formally retain the presidency. Portes Gil replaced him, but Calles, the "Jefe Máximo", retained effective political power during what is known as the Maximato.

Positions held: Member of the Chamber of Deputies of Mexico

Q428598.label: 2005 United Kingdom general election
Q428598.desc: election of members to the House of Commons in 2005
Q428598.summary: A general election was held in the United Kingdom on 5 May 2005, to elect 646 members to the House of Commons. The governing Labour Party led by Prime Minister Tony Blair won its third consecutive victory, with Blair becoming the second Labour leader after Harold Wilson to form three majority governments.

Q3706934.desc: To permit the state to ratify the Treaty of Amsterdam
aliases: 18th Amendment of the Constitution of Ireland
Q3706934.wiki: Eighteenth Amendment of the Constitution of Ireland
Q3706934.summary: The Eighteenth Amendment of the Constitution Act 1998 is an amendment of the Constitution of Ireland which permitted the state to ratify the Treaty of Amsterdam. It was approved by referendum on 22 May 1998 and signed into law on the 3 June of the same year.

Q62574646.label: Thirty-eighth Amendment of the Constitution 2016
Q62574646.wiki: Thirty-eighth Amendment of the Constitution of Ireland
Q62574646.summary: The Thirty-eighth Amendment of the Constitution of Ireland is an amendment to the Constitution of Ireland which altered the provisions regulating divorce. It removed the constitutional requirement for a defined period of separation before a Court may grant a dissolution of marriage, and eased restrictions on the recognition of foreign divorces.

Q2580534.label: 1932 Belgian general election
Q2580534.summary: General elections were held in Belgium on 27 November 1932. The Catholic Party won 79 of the 187 seats in the Chamber of Representatives and 42 of the 93 seats in the Senate. Voter turnout was 94.3%.

Q1542710.label: Radical Party
Q1542710.desc: liberal and centrist political party in France
Q1542710.summary: The Radical Party, officially the Republican, Radical and Radical-Socialist Party, is a liberal and social-liberal political party in France. Since 1971, to prevent confusion with the Radical Party of the Left (PRG), it has also been referred to as Parti radical valoisien, after its headquarters on the rue de Valois. The party's name has been variously abbreviated to PRRRS, Rad, PR and PRV. Founded in 1901, the PR is the oldest active political party in France.

Member of: Alliance of Liberals and Democrats for Europe Party

Q57398.label: Aníbal Cavaco Silva
Q57398.summary: Aníbal António Cavaco Silva is a Portuguese economist and politician who served as the president of Portugal from 2006 to 2016, and as prime minister of Portugal, from 1985 to 1995. His 10-year tenure was the longest of any prime minister since Salazar, and the longest for a freely elected prime minister in Portugal's republican history.

Q710198.label: Māris Gailis
Q710198.summary: Māris Gailis is a Latvian businessman and former politician. He is the former prime minister of Latvia, an office he held from September 1994 to December 1995.

Q950326.label: Tongmenghui
Q950326.img: Sun Yat Sen together with the members of the Singapore Branch of Tongmen Hui.png
Q950326.summary: The Tongmenghui of China was a secret society and underground resistance movement founded by Sun Yat-sen, Song Jiaoren, and others in Tokyo, Empire of Japan, on 20 August 1905, with the goal of overthrowing China's Qing dynasty. It was formed from the merger of multiple late-Qing dynasty Chinese revolutionary groups.

Q14605366.label: Brussels Agreement
Q14605366.desc: 2013 agreement to normalize relations between Serbia and Kosovo
aliases: First agreement of principles governing the normalisation of relations
Q14605366.summary: The First Agreement of Principles Governing the Normalisation of Relations, informally known as the Brussels Agreement, is an agreement to normalize relations between the governments of Serbia and Kosovo. The agreement, negotiated and concluded in Brussels under the auspices of the European Union, was signed on 19 April 2013.

Q4871734.label: Battle of Mikołów
Q4871734.summary: The Battle of Mikołów refers to the border engagement on September 1 and 2, 1939, that took place in the area of the town of Mikołów, located in the Silesian Voivodeship, during the early stages of the Invasion of Poland in the Second World War.

Q218678.label: North African campaign
Q218678.desc: 194–1943 military campaign of World War II
Q218678.summary: The North African campaign of World War II took place in North Africa from 11 June 1940 to 13 May 1943, fought between the Allies and the Axis powers. It included campaigns in the Libyan and Egyptian deserts, in Morocco and Algeria, and in Tunisia. The Allied war effort was dominated by the British Commonwealth and exiles from German-occupied Europe. The United States entered the war in December 1941 and began direct military assistance in North Africa on 11 May 1942.

Q4382262.label: First Battle of Târgu Frumos
Q4382262.img: Bundesarchiv Bild 183-J24359, Rumänien, Kolonne von Panzer V (Panther).jpg
Q4382262.summary: The First Battle of Târgu Frumos was fought during World War II between Axis powers commanded by Otto Wöhler and Soviet forces led by Ivan Konev. Historian David Glantz has described it as part of a failed Soviet invasion of Romania, while Russian and German sources have described it as part of the Târgu Frumos Operation.

Q7097398.label: Operation Pistol
Q7097398.desc: WW2 SAS operation in occupied France (Oct 1944)
Q7097398.summary: Operation Pistol was the code name for a Special Air Service mission during the Second World War, with the objective to parachute four teams from 'A' Squadron 2nd Special Air Service behind the German lines around the Alsace–Lorraine region of France. Once on the ground they would attempt to disrupt the road and rail networks between Metz and Nancy and the approach to the Rhine plain.

Q3616310.label: Battle of Phuoc Long
Q3616310.desc: 1974 decisive battle of the Vietnam War
Q3616310.img: Map of the Battle of Phuoc Long.jpg
Q3616310.summary: The Battle of Phước Long was a decisive battle of the Vietnam War which began on 12 December 1974, and concluded on 6 January 1975. The battle involved the deployment of the People's Army of Vietnam (PAVN) 4th Army Corps for the first time, against units of the Army of the Republic of Vietnam (ARVN) in Phước Long in Bình Phước Province near the Cambodian border, under the command of Lieutenant General Dư Quốc Đống.

Q817206.label: Cambodian Civil War
Q817206.desc: civil war in Cambodia between 1967 and 1975
Q817206.summary: The Cambodian Civil War was a civil war in Cambodia fought by the Khmer Rouge against the government of the Kingdom of Cambodia. Following the March 1970 coup, the conflict shifted as the Khmer Rouge and forces loyal to Norodom Sihanouk, now supported by North Vietnam and China, fought against the Khmer Republic, which was supported by the United States and South Vietnam.

Participants: National Liberation Front of South Vietnam

Q4594742.summary: The Grozny refugee convoy shooting occurred on 3 December 1999, when at least 40 people fleeing the besieged Chechen capital Grozny were reportedly killed by Russian special police units, OMON.

Q1893430.summary: The Reform Party of the United States of America (RPUSA), generally known as the Reform Party USA or the Reform Party, is a centrist political party in the United States. The party was founded in 1995 by Ross Perot and qualifies as a third party.

Q827958.label: British Columbia Social Credit Party
Q827958.summary: The British Columbia Social Credit Party was a conservative political party in British Columbia, Canada. It was the governing party of British Columbia for all but three years between the 1952 provincial election and the 1991 election. For four decades, the party dominated the British Columbian political scene, with the only break occurring between the 1972 and 1975 elections when the British Columbia New Democratic Party governed. Party members were known as Socreds.
